raw_document.title: EpsilonGen Receives FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation for EGX-502 in ALS
raw_document.raw_text:
EpsilonGen Therapeutics (NASDAQ: EPSG) today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation (BTD) to EGX-502 (epsilotide) for the treatment of adults with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Breakthrough Therapy Designation is granted to expedite the development and review of drugs that are intended to treat a serious condition and preliminary clinical evidence indicates the drug may demonstrate substantial improvement over available therapies on a clinically significant endpoint.

The BTD was supported by data from the Phase 2 ADVANCE trial (NCT03987654), which demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in disease progression compared to placebo, as measured by the ALSFRS-R total score at 24 weeks.

'The Breakthrough Therapy Designation underscores the FDA's recognition of EGX-502's potential to transform treatment for ALS patients,' said Dr. Michael Chen, Chief Scientific Officer of EpsilonGen. 'We will work closely with the FDA to accelerate development and bring EGX-502 to patients as rapidly as possible.'

EGX-502 is a first-in-class antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) targeting SOD1. The company expects to initiate a Phase 3 trial in mid-2024.
